records.region: Northern Chile, Arica y Parinacota and the Tarapacá boundary; Macusa–Ajatama headward corridor and Camarones receiving valley to the Pacific coast.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported receiving-river identity for the western and coastal course; proposed representative identity remains incomplete because the chosen headward opening lacks source correspondence.
records.material_pending_reason: A short northern headward interval from the chosen opening to the beginning of the mapped Macusa course has no acquired primary source establishing its watercourse correspondence. The distinct named downstream components do not close that gap.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected northern opening descends southeast and south along Macusa, turns west onto Ajatama, remains north of the separate Caritaya reservoir approach, continues west and southwest along Camarones, passes the Chiza junction near Cuya, and terminates at the coastal Camarones wetland/mouth setting.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research is finished with one material-pending primary state. Distinct Macusa, Ajatama and Camarones components can form a representative receiving system, but the missing headward link prevents completed full-selection correspondence. The coastal terminal is geographically accounted for without precise present shoreline or flow claims.
records.supported_name_scope: Río Macusa on the mapped northern descending component; Río Ajatama on the selected upper westward course; Río Camarones on the middle and lower receiving corridor to the coastal wetland. These are component names, not synonyms or a scalar name imposed on every stored part.

scope_limits: The chosen northern opening remains a genuine source-material gap; it is not merely an unnamed reach on an otherwise completely proved selected path.
The distinct component names do not establish a uniform whole-route hydronym or an adjudicated transition point.
The terminal finding concerns the Camarones coastal wetland/mouth corridor, not a present open outlet, exact beach crossing or current flow regime.
No official source-point designation, full irrigation-work inventory, reservoir operation or formal registry/Korean name is established.
The municipal plan and natural-watercourse layer use differing northern tributary spellings; no official alias equivalence is inferred.

records.region: Maranhão; São Gonçalo / Campineira–Rio Palmeira–Rio Preguiças–Barreirinhas–lower estuary coastal setting
records.candidate_name_role: Provisional representative receiving-system identity with a distinct named upper reach
records.material_pending_reason: The selected final northeastward estuary-to-Atlantic extension crosses the mapped coastal dune/barrier setting southeast of the depicted Preguiças inlet. No inspected original establishes that actual selected through-link. This is a material terminal connection gap, not a requirement for exact banks, contemporary discharge or a uniformly named river.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Rio Preguiças identifies the mapped connected middle/lower river and estuary. The selected upper approach includes Rio Palmeira and an unnamed small headward feeder. The actual final selected coastward through-link remains unsupported; the candidate is not a completed whole-feature identity.
records.completion_scope: All 42 stored parts across both stages were considered. Opening, upper Palmeira, Preguiças joining and middle/lower course, Barreirinhas fragment join and broad estuarine passage are supported at ordinary source-correspondence scale. The actual final coastal through-link remains pending.
records.supported_name_scope: Mapped river reaches and representative receiving-system context only. No single hydronym is imposed on the headward feeder, all tributaries, wetland components or final coastal extension.

scope_limits: The final selected coastward extension is a genuine source-to-route through-link gap. The documented northern inlet cannot be substituted merely because both reach the Atlantic.
The municipal maps are generalized multi-source compilations; individual current banks, tides, discharge, navigability and exact hydronym-change vertices are outside scope.
Costa2025 documents inlet/spit migration in the depicted northern mouth area. That finding does not prove a channel at a different selected barrier crossing or present conditions in2026.
No scalar whole-system name, Korean name, formal registry verification or product application is supported by this research result.

records.region: Washington, United States: Mount Rainier, White River, lower Puyallup River and Tacoma/Commencement Bay
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-system identity for the connected Emmons Glacier–White River–lower Puyallup route to Commencement Bay. The long upper and middle selected reach is White River, while Puyallup River is directly supported for the receiving lower reach. Neither river name is imposed as a scalar over the glacier, adjoining tributaries, lake features or port waterways.
records.completion_scope: Both mainstem fragments and all 49 selected parts have ordinary source correspondence: Emmons glacial drainage to White River, its continuous middle-valley passage, lower Puyallup receiving junction and actual Puyallup Waterway/Commencement Bay terminal. Unverified management labels or operating details do not create a missing through-link where the selected channel is continuously mapped.
records.supported_name_scope: NPS identifies Emmons meltwater as the White River source; the original maps show White River joining Puyallup River and the lower river reaching Puyallup Waterway/Commencement Bay. Pierce County independently identifies the regional Puyallup-White watershed. The system finding does not assert that the entire selected line is locally named Puyallup River.

scope_limits: Formal registry status and Korean rendering were not verified.
The initial selected glacier segment has representative glacial-drainage correspondence, not proof of a continuous exposed or subglacial natural river channel.

Explicit Mud Mountain dam/reservoir name, pool extent and management/operating details remain unverified in the actually read material. The selected mapped White River through-link is nevertheless continuous.
The maps are generalized and multitemporal. Their bank positions, channels and glacier depiction are not asserted to be a present operational survey.
Lake Tapps is a separate mapped side waterbody; no hydraulic operation or water-transfer schedule is established.
Puyallup Waterway identifies the terminal mapped port-channel setting; its boundaries are not imposed on the generalized endpoint.
